name: field
title: Field
description: One thing a player types or ticks, with its label, its requirement and its reason. BDS-040 is the visible rule and it rides `data-gs-elevation`: a text, email, tel, password or number field is `inset` and a checkbox or radio is `raised`, so a player can tell what they type into from what they press. It validates nothing: `invalid` is the host's word and `reason` is the host's sentence, carried to a screen reader through `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` rather than only shown. Required and optional are words on screen plus `aria-required`, never an asterisk and never a colour. A consent box is never pre-checked by the component. One value out of a known set is `selector`, not this.
docs: Pass `name`, `label` and the `control` the player works: `text` is the default, `checkbox` and `radio` are pressed and render raised. Pass `requirement` to state required or optional in words. Pass `invalid` and `reason` together when your own validation fails a value; the field never decides that itself, and a `reason` on its own is a rule explained rather than a failure. Anything else you pass reaches the `<input>`, so `value`, `onChange`, `placeholder`, `inputMode` and `autoComplete` all work as they do on a native control. Find a field with `[data-gs-field="<name>"]` and its control with `[data-gs-part="control"]`.
